cards.title: IBeam COM 001: Define commerce offers and total-seat pricing
cards.description:
Add provider-neutral offer and pricing models that map a public plan selection to product, plan, billing interval, currency, and total seat quantity.

Acceptance criteria:
- An individual offer has one license and one total seat by default.
- A multi-user offer has one license and a minimum of three total seats.
- Provider quantity means total seats, not additional seats.
- Pricing supports base, per-seat, tiered, and provider price references without provider SDK dependencies.
- Tests cover individual purchase, three-seat purchase, expansion, invalid quantities, and normalization.

cards.title: IBeam COM 002: Add stable GUID license keys and lookup
cards.description:
Expose a stable GUID-backed license key for support, claiming, lookup, and cross-provider correlation without exposing storage partition details.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every new license has a non-empty immutable GUID license key.
- Existing records receive a backward-compatible key or migration strategy.
- Services resolve licenses by key with tenant authorization where required.
- Public responses expose only the safe key.
- Tests cover uniqueness, lookup, compatibility, and tenant isolation.

cards.title: IBeam COM 003: Add provider-neutral checkout gateway contracts
cards.description:
Define checkout, customer-portal, webhook-verification, and provider-binding contracts so hosts select a processor through dependency injection and configuration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contracts cover checkout, provider status, portal sessions, and webhook verification.
- Requests use offer keys, total seats, correlation ids, and allow-listed return URLs.
- Results contain provider-neutral status and opaque references.
- Core Billing does not reference a provider SDK.
- Tests use two fake providers to prove replaceability.

cards.title: IBeam COM 004: Model purchases before Identity or tenant exists
cards.description:
Add a pending purchase aggregate that records a public buyer and paid offer before an IBeam user or tenant exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pending purchases use GUID ids and may omit tenant id and user id.
- Records capture normalized email, offer, total seats, provider binding, amounts, currency, status, and timestamps.
- Statuses cover initiated through paid, fulfilled, claimed, expired, canceled, refunded, and failed.
- Duplicate events cannot create duplicate purchases or licenses.
- PII retention, redaction, expiration, and tests are included.

cards.title: IBeam COM 005: Add public checkout and purchase-status API
cards.description:
Expose anonymous-safe endpoints to start checkout and report limited purchase status without an existing Identity account.

Acceptance criteria:
- POST /api/commerce/checkout-sessions validates offer and total seats, creates a pending purchase, and returns hosted checkout URL.
- GET /api/commerce/purchases/{purchaseId}/status returns safe next-action data using a protected correlation token.
- Success and cancel URLs are allow-listed.
- Rate limits, idempotency, anti-enumeration, and structured errors are included.
- Tests cover highest-plan checkout with three total seats and no tenant or user.

cards.title: IBeam COM 006: Normalize verified provider webhooks
cards.description:
Verify provider signatures, record events idempotently, and map processor payloads into normalized commerce events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unverified payloads never mutate Billing or Licensing.
- Events cover completion, payment success/failure, renewal, seat change, cancellation, refund, and dispute.
- Processing is idempotent by provider and event id.
- Browser redirects do not fulfill purchases.
- Tests cover replay, ordering, invalid signatures, retries, and unsupported events.

cards.title: IBeam COM 007: Add optional Stripe billing adapter
cards.description:
Implement Stripe as the first optional checkout and webhook adapter without adding Stripe dependencies to provider-neutral packages.

Acceptance criteria:
- A separate adapter implements checkout and webhook contracts.
- Metadata carries IBeam purchase id, offer key, and total seats.
- Stripe quantity maps to total seats including the minimum three.
- Keys and webhook secrets come from host secret configuration and are never logged.
- Tests cover checkout, completion, renewal, seat change, cancellation, and replay.

cards.title: IBeam COM 008: Fulfill paid purchases into one license
cards.description:
Turn a normalized paid purchase into one durable license with the selected plan and total seat limit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fulfillment creates exactly one license regardless of seat count.
- Individual purchases create one seat; multi-user purchases create at least three total seats.
- Repeated fulfillment returns the same license.
- Provider references are replaceable bindings, not license identity.
- Tests cover first purchase, replay, three seats, and expansion.

cards.title: IBeam COM 009: Add secure purchase claim and onboarding flow
cards.description:
Let a buyer sign up or sign in, create or select a tenant, and securely claim a paid license.

Acceptance criteria:
- One-time expiring claim tokens are separate from GUID license keys and stored hashed.
- Claiming links purchase, billing, license, tenant, and buyer recoverably.
- The verified buyer receives the first seat and remaining seats stay available.
- Claims reject reuse, wrong buyer, expiration, and cross-tenant takeover.
- Tests cover new and existing users, retries, expiration, and three-seat onboarding.

cards.title: IBeam COM 010: Reconcile renewals, seat changes, and cancellations
cards.description:
Update the existing license when a provider subscription renews or changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Renewal preserves the same license GUID key and assignments.
- Seat increases update total seats; decreases below assignments use an explicit over-assigned policy.
- Individual licenses can expand and multi-user plans retain a minimum of three.
- Cancellation, failed payment, refund, and grace behavior are policy driven.
- Tests cover each lifecycle path without replacement licenses.

cards.title: IBeam COM 011: Support payment-provider migration
cards.description:
Move a tenant subscription from Stripe to PayPal or another processor while retaining the same internal history and license.

Acceptance criteria:
- Internal billing, purchase, subscription, and license ids remain provider-neutral.
- Licenses retain historical bindings and one active provider binding.
- Migration avoids access gaps and double grants.
- Idempotency is provider scoped and reconciliation prevents duplicate renewals.
- Stripe-like and PayPal-like fake adapters prove the license and seats survive migration.

cards.title: IBeam COM 012: Persist checkout, purchase, claim, and provider bindings
cards.description:
Extend durable commerce storage with pending purchases, checkout attempts, claim records, and provider-binding indexes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Azure Tables support lookup by GUID purchase/license key and provider references.
- State transitions use optimistic concurrency and safe retries.
- Claim and fulfillment idempotency survive restarts.
- Tokens are hashed and raw provider bodies are excluded from public records.
- Tests cover persistence, concurrency, replay, lookup, and expired-purchase cleanup.

cards.title: IBeam COM 013: Add commerce administration and recovery APIs
cards.description:
Provide protected support/admin endpoints to inspect commerce state and recover failed fulfillment safely.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admins inspect purchase, billing, license, seat, claim, and provider-binding status.
- Support retries verified event processing or fulfillment without resubmitting payment.
- Resending onboarding creates a new claim token and invalidates the old one.
- Manual corrections require authorization, reason, audit, and idempotency.
- Responses redact secrets, provider payloads, and unnecessary PII.

cards.title: IBeam COM 014: Add end-to-end commerce validation and guide
cards.description:
Validate and document public purchase, Identity onboarding, seat fulfillment, and provider portability.

Acceptance criteria:
- E2E buys the highest plan with three total seats before Identity exists, verifies payment, creates one license, claims it, and assigns the buyer.
- Tests cover one-seat expansion, replay, failed payment, cancellation, and provider migration.
- Docs map public/admin endpoints with DTOs and sequence diagrams.
- Guidance separates checkout UI, Billing, Licensing, Identity, and runtime enforcement.
- Security guidance covers redirects, signatures, idempotency, claim tokens, PII, secrets, and audit.
